# `oled_ctrl` register map

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_regmap.py from regmap/oled_ctrl.yaml. Do not edit. -->

Text-mode display controller. The PL owns the panel: it runs the power-up sequence, holds a character framebuffer in block RAM, and refreshes the display autonomously, so the screen never goes blank when host software stops. The host owns the words: it writes ASCII into character RAM through CURSOR/CHAR, and live ADC and DAC values are formatted to ASCII by the host and written the same way. Three panels are supported by one engine: SSD1306 over SPI (PmodOLED, 128x32), SSD1331 over SPI (PmodOLEDrgb, 96x64), and SSD1306 over I2C (bare 4-pin modules).

6 registers, 24 bytes.

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description |
| ------ | ---- | ------ | ----- | ----------- |
| `0x00` | `CTRL` | rw | `0x00000000` | Run control. INIT and CLEAR are write-1-to-act and clear themselves. |
| `0x04` | `CFG` | rw | `0x00000404` | Panel type and interface timing. |
| `0x08` | `CURSOR` | rw | `0x00000000` | Character-RAM write pointer. CHAR writes land here and then advance it, so a whole line is one register write per character with no address bookkeeping on the host side. |
| `0x0C` | `CHAR` | rw | `0x00000000` | Write an ASCII character at CURSOR and advance the cursor. Writing four packed characters at once is supported via COUNT, which is how the host pushes a whole string with one word per four characters. |
| `0x10` | `GEOMETRY` | ro | `0x00000000` | Character grid implied by the selected panel and font. The host reads this instead of hard-coding it. |
| `0x14` | `STATUS` | ro | `0x00000000` | Live engine state. |

## `CTRL` (`0x00`, rw)

Run control. INIT and CLEAR are write-1-to-act and clear themselves.

| Bits | Field | Description |
| ---- | ----- | ----------- |
| `4` | `DISP_ON` | Panel display-on. Clearing it blanks the panel without losing character RAM. |
| `3` | `INVERT` | Inverse video. |
| `2` | `CLEAR` | Self-clearing: fill character RAM with spaces. |
| `1` | `INIT` | Self-clearing: re-run the panel power-on and configuration sequence. |
| `0` | `ENABLE` | Enable the refresh engine. |

## `CFG` (`0x04`, rw)

Panel type and interface timing.

| Bits | Field | Description |
| ---- | ----- | ----------- |
| `31:24` | `CONTRAST` | Panel contrast |
| `22:16` | `I2C_ADDR` | 7-bit I2C slave address when PANEL = 2. Typically 0x3C. |
| `15:8` | `CLK_DIV` | Serial half-period in aclk cycles minus one |
| `1:0` | `PANEL` | 0 = SSD1306 SPI 128x32, 1 = SSD1331 SPI 96x64, 2 = SSD1306 I2C. |

## `CURSOR` (`0x08`, rw)

Character-RAM write pointer. CHAR writes land here and then advance it, so a whole line is one register write per character with no address bookkeeping on the host side.

| Bits | Field | Description |
| ---- | ----- | ----------- |
| `16` | `WRAP` | Advance to the next row at end of line rather than clamping. |
| `15:8` | `ROW` | Character row |
| `7:0` | `COL` | Character column |

## `CHAR` (`0x0C`, rw)

Write an ASCII character at CURSOR and advance the cursor. Writing four packed characters at once is supported via COUNT, which is how the host pushes a whole string with one word per four characters.

| Bits | Field | Description |
| ---- | ----- | ----------- |
| `31:24` | `C3` | Fourth character. |
| `23:16` | `C2` | Third character. |
| `15:8` | `C1` | Second character. |
| `7:0` | `C0` | First character. |

## `GEOMETRY` (`0x10`, ro)

Character grid implied by the selected panel and font. The host reads this instead of hard-coding it.

| Bits | Field | Description |
| ---- | ----- | ----------- |
| `31:24` | `FONT_H` | Font cell height in pixels. |
| `23:16` | `FONT_W` | Font cell width in pixels. |
| `15:8` | `ROWS` | Character rows. |
| `7:0` | `COLS` | Character columns. |

## `STATUS` (`0x14`, ro)

Live engine state.

| Bits | Field | Description |
| ---- | ----- | ----------- |
| `31:8` | `FRAME_COUNT` | Completed refresh frames since reset. A stalled count means the panel is not being driven. |
| `1` | `INIT_DONE` | The panel init sequence has completed at least once. |
| `0` | `BUSY` | A serial transfer is in progress. |
